claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the current model release is compliant and evidentially supported under the model-card disclosure policy.

concern_ledger.concern: Current release documentation is not shown to reflect the current evaluation results, including the Spanish-language billing regression.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Admissible current release documentation or model-card text showing the current evaluation results and subgroup weakness are incorporated.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The policy makes current-release documentation a prerequisite to certification.

concern_ledger.concern: The Spanish-language billing support weakness appears material for a named launch use case and is not shown as disclosed or resolved.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Admissible evidence of explicit disclosure in the release documentation or evidence the weakness was resolved before launch.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The policy requires disclosure or approved mitigation for material segment weaknesses before certification.

concern_ledger.concern: No reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or approved risk acceptance is attached; only an informal monitoring comment exists.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: An admissible approved mitigation plan, formal owner acceptance, or risk-acceptance record tied to this release.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: Informal monitoring does not satisfy the policy requirement for approved mitigation or risk acceptance.

concern_ledger.concern: The actor relies in part on prior approval of the same model family, but that approval predates the relevant update and eval batch.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Admissible current-release approval materials reviewed after the locale-routing update and current evaluation batch.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: Stale approval cannot supply the current evidence the policy requires for this release.

decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results.
Material segment weaknesses for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved before launch.
If not resolved, a reviewed and approved mitigation or risk acceptance must exist before certification.
Prior approvals and informal monitoring notes may provide context but cannot substitute for current evidence or reviewed risk acceptance.
evidence_requests: Provide the current release model card or release documentation showing the Spanish-language billing support weakness is explicitly disclosed for the named launch use case.
Provide an approved mitigation or formal risk-acceptance record covering the current subgroup regression before launch.
Provide evidence that current evaluation results, including the locale-routing update effects, are reflected in the certification packet reviewed for this release.
specific_concerns: The policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results, but no admissible evidence shows the current release documentation was updated to include the current subgroup regression.
The Spanish-language billing support slice is below the warning threshold for a named launch use case, and the policy requires disclosure or approved mitigation before certification.
The only cited operational response is an informal post-launch monitoring comment; admissible evidence says there is no reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language attached.
Prior approval of the same model family is stale contextual evidence because it predates the locale-routing update and current evaluation batch.
unsupported_claims: The recommendation to certify is not supported by admissible evidence because the required current-release disclosure or approved mitigation is missing.
Any implication that informal monitoring can close the policy gap is unsupported by the admissible evidence.
Any implication that prior approval materially supports current certification is unsupported beyond background context.
